title: The Cover of Marseille's old port
premise: Juniper Sterling's spotless career laundering audits is a cover for a life she fled in Marseille a decade ago. When a stranger repays a favor she never performed, she learns her old mentor faked the debt to summon her back: he needs her to extract Nadia Rahal, a defector carrying proof that a European bank laundered cartel money through Marseille's old port. But Nadia may be bait set by the very network Juniper once escaped, and every ally — including the mentor — has a price. Juniper must choose between burning the truth wide open and protecting the few people who ever belonged to her; in the end she exposes the bank at devastating personal cost, walks away from justice's official channels, and finally stops running.
about_author: Lena Voss spent seven years working compliance desks in port cities before trading ledgers for fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose clean lives are built on buried ones, and lives within sight of water she doesn't swim in.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In London, Juniper audits a hedge fund so pristine it makes her itch; that night she checks the go-bag by her door out of habit. A courier delivers an envelope containing a photo of her at nineteen, on Marseille's docks, and a note: 'You're owed nothing. You owe everything.' The beat: dread dressed as routine.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She traces the courier to a shuttered café near the Vieux-Port and confronts Étienne Marchand, her old mentor, who admits he invented the debt to force her home. He shows her Nadia Rahal: a bank insider hiding in Marseille with ledger proof of cartel flows. Beat: fury curdling into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Old Port, Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Walking the quays she grew up on, she maps the bank's shell companies against places she knows too well — including the fish market where her brother died. Étienne warns her the network remembers faces. Beat: belonging as both comfort and trap.

chapters.title: Nadia
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Hiding above a dive shop, Nadia watches her handlers' surveillance tighten and tests Juniper when they meet, feeding her one true detail and one false one. She needs extraction to Barcelona in seventy-two hours. Beat: mutual suspicion sharpening into necessity.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper verifies part of Nadia's ledger but finds a transaction dated three days before Nadia claims to have copied it — someone inside the bank knew about the leak early. She begins to suspect Nadia is being used as bait to draw out whoever ordered the original favor. Beat: the ground tilting.

chapters.title: The Fish Market
chapters.summary: Étienne's POV. Étienne meets his old contact Colonel Ferrand to buy safe passage, and realizes Ferrand already knows Nadia's name — meaning the leak runs through him. He lies to protect Juniper, repeating the sin that broke them apart years ago. Beat: loyalty as betrayal in slow motion.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The extraction plan launches by fishing boat, but Juniper confronts Nadia mid-route with the timeline discrepancy. Nadia confesses: the bank offered her freedom if she lured out 'the person who took the original ledger' — Étienne. Beat: trust shattered at sea, engines idling toward a decision.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Keeps
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV (climax). Ambushed at a cove, Juniper turns the trap: she broadcasts the real ledger to journalists and regulators simultaneously, making herself worthless as leverage. Ferrand's men take Étienne instead; Nadia chooses to stay and testify rather than vanish. Beat: truth deployed as a weapon, costing everything it should.

chapters.title: The Price of Light
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The story breaks; the bank burns, Ferrand is arrested, and Étienne trades names for a reduced sentence, refusing to see her. Nadia, in protective custody, sends Juniper the one page of the ledger that mentions her brother's death. Beat: justice achieved outside the law, grief arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Months later, Juniper testifies not as an investigator but as a witness, then resigns. She unpacks the go-bag for the first time in ten years, keeps only her brother's photograph, and stays in Marseille — not because she belongs, but because she stopped needing to. Beat: quiet, earned resolution.
